At Phillip Riley we are looking for an experienced Geotechnical Engineer to join our team.

As the Geotechnical Engineer you will be responsible for dealing with the mechanics of soil and rock and its applications to engineering elements.

Main tasks will include:

You will deal with the analysis, design and construction of man-made structures or systems that are made of or are supported by soil or rock.
Identify, design and implement practical solutions to engineering problems concerning soil, rock and groundwater.
Apply scientific and engineering techniques to predict and manage the behaviour of the ground where it interacts with or responds to human activity.
Plan, direct and conduct survey work to analyse the likely behaviour of soil and rock when placed under pressure by proposed structures, and designs above and below ground foundations.
Obtaining soil and rock samples at different depths across sites and testing samples to determine strength, compressibility and other factors that affect the behaviour of soil and rock when a structure is imposed and determining the safe loading for the soil
Plans, directs and conducts survey work to analyse the likely behaviour of soil and rock when placed under pressure by proposed structures, and designs above and below ground foundations
Key skills:

Problem solving
Communication
Project management
Teamwork
Analytical abilities
Soil mechanics
Adaptability
Analysis
Data collection
Research
Slope stability
Environmental and geographical factors
Geotechnical analysis
Ability to apply technical knowledge
Ensure compliance with all regulatory standards
Geotechnical design
Minimum of 1 year experience required

Please note that only successful candidates will be contacted.

Salary $87,500 - $107,500 + Superannuation

Worrells is a fast growing, specialist accounting firm with expertise in solvency management and insolvency administration. We have carved a successful niche in the small to medium enterprise market by delivering quality service and processes with our unique systems. Established in 1973, Worrells now have 36 principals in 28 locations across NSW, QLD, ACT, VIC and WA, we draw upon broader resources and technical expertise enabling us to be focused locally while being resourced nationally.

We are looking for a full time Insolvency Accountant to join our NSW/ACT team based in Parramatta NSW. The successful candidate will be responsible for:

Day to day file management of insolvency appointments (from start to finish)
Preparation of statutory lodgements
Liaising with directors, employees, creditors, banks, statutory authorities and other stakeholders
Collection and investigation into records
Prioritise and manage workloads to meet conflicting deadlines
Analyse financial statements and diverse financial data
Drafting of reports and preparation of creditors meetings
Investigations into insolvent trading, voidable transactions and offences committed by officers
Attending sites to inspect, collect and record assets and books and records
Assisting with Fair Entitlements Guarantee claims and calculating employee entitlements.

We are seeking a candidate who has:

Proficient knowledge of Microsoft Office (Words, Excel, Outlook)
A Bachelor Degree or equivalent in Commerce, Finance or Accounting
Excellent communication skills (both written and verbal)
CA or CPA qualified (or willing to obtain)
ARITA Introduction to Insolvency certification
ARITA professional qualification (or willing to obtain)
Previous experience in insolvency is required.

We understand the importance of work-life balance, and we offer flexibility to support your needs. You'll become part of a collaborative team of professionals who are dedicated to both their work and personal growth. We provide opportunities for ongoing learning and development, and you'll have access to resources that will help you advance in your career. Worrells is committed to your professional growth, and we'll provide the support you need to succeed.

result.description:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a highly skilled Database Developer to join a forward-thinking educational institution in Perth.   This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working across SQL Server, integrations, reporting, and application development, with the opportunity to have a real impact on how data is used across the business.  
      This role sits at the heart of the Information and Learning Technologies team, where your technical expertise will directly support both business and academic operations. You will be instrumental in designing, developing, and maintaining robust data solutions and digital applications that underpin the organisation's strategic goals. This position offers you the chance to work closely with stakeholders across the school community, ensuring reliable, secure, and scalable technology outcomes. The role is perfect for someone who thrives in a supportive environment that values knowledge sharing, professional growth, and making a tangible impact on student wellbeing 
 
 Play a key role in shaping data-driven decision-making by developing integrated solutions that enhance accessibility, reporting, and analytics across the institution. 
 Enjoy flexible working opportunities within a collaborative team that values professional development, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement. 
 Make a real difference by supporting student wellbeing and academic success through innovative use of technology and data intelligence. 
 
     
  Responsibilities:  
     
 
 Serve as the primary system administrator and subject-matter expert for the key projects, overseeing configuration, user management, data integrity, version upgrades, and module administration. 
 Design, maintain, and optimise database schemas and SQL Server infrastructure to ensure high performance, availability, security, and data quality across all systems. 
 Architect, develop, and manage integrations between core CRM platforms, finance systems, cloud identity providers, and communication tools using APIs (REST/SOAP), middleware, and ETL processes. 
 Develop dashboards, reports, self-service analytics tools, and custom queries using platforms like Power BI, Crystal Reports, SSRS or similar to support strategic planning and operational needs. 
 Champion data quality frameworks by implementing profiling, cleansing, validation routines, and advising stakeholders on evidence-based decision-making. 
 Administer database change management processes including updates, release procedures, backup/recovery strategies while ensuring compliance with privacy legislation and organisational policies. 
 Design, develop, test, deploy and maintain custom web applications or internal tools using modern frameworks (Python/.NET/Node.js) aligned with the institution's technology stack. 
 Collaborate with stakeholders from various departments to gather requirements for digital solutions that extend enterprise system capabilities while ensuring secure coding practices are followed. 
 Create comprehensive technical documentation in partnership with key stakeholders; utilise ticketing systems for request tracking; document all changes thoroughly before implementation. 
 
 Mentor IT staff in best practices for database management and application development while staying abreast of emerging technologies. 
 
 
  Requirements:  
 
 Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering or related discipline is essential for this role. 
 Advanced proficiency in Microsoft SQL Server technologies including T-SQL scripting, query optimisation techniques as well as experience with SSIS/SSRS or equivalent reporting tools is required. 
 Demonstrated ability to design API-based or middleware integrations (REST/SOAP/webhooks/ETL/Wonde) along with strong skills in ASP.NET/PowerShell/scripting languages is necessary. 
 Solid application development experience using one or more programming languages such as Python/C#/.NET/Node.js/PHP is expected. 
 Proven track record delivering business intelligence solutions using Power BI/Tableau/SSRS/Microsoft Fabric/Crystal Reports or similar platforms is highly valued. 
 Comprehensive understanding of data governance principles including privacy legislation (Australian Privacy Act/APP) plus information security best practices is mandatory. 
 Minimum five years experience in senior database administration or application development roles ideally within education or enterprise environments is preferred. 
 Excellent business analysis skills encompassing risk assessment solution design capabilities coupled with outstanding troubleshooting/problem-solving abilities are vital. 
 Exceptional communication skills enabling clear translation of technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders alongside proven stakeholder engagement experience are important attributes. 
 A positive outlook combined with willingness to embrace organisational values around service/integrity/stewardship plus demonstrated commitment to health & safety policies is expected. 
    Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples are encouraged to apply.  
 To apply please click apply or call  Milena Wawrzyniak-Kalyanpur on +61 8 9266 0980 for a confidential discussion.

result.description:
Lead Safety. Build Culture. Make a Real Difference.

Are you a passionate safety professional who knows that great safety outcomes are built on trust, influence and genuine engagement with people?

We are seeking an experienced Safety Manager to join a diverse and growing organisation based in Wangaratta, supporting a workforce of approximately 300 employees across multiple operational environments including manufacturing, warehousing and field-based technical services.

This is an opportunity to step into a highly visible leadership role where you will shape safety strategy, influence business performance and help create a workplace where everyone goes home safe every day.

About the Role

Reporting to senior leadership, you will lead and drive the Health, Safety and Wellbeing function across multiple sites and operational activities. You will develop, implement and continuously improve safety systems, ensuring compliance while fostering a practical, positive and people-focused safety culture.

You will be responsible for:

* Developing, implementing and managing the organisation's OHS Operational Plan
* Acting as the organisation's Return to Work (RTW) Coordinator
* Leading risk management activities, including hazard identification, risk assessments and controls
* Delivering and coordinating safety training, coaching and capability development
* Supporting managers and employees with task design, reasonable adjustments and injury prevention initiatives
* Facilitating meaningful consultation with employees, Health and Safety Representatives and key stakeholders
* Leading incident investigations using recognised methodologies such as ICAM, Root Cause Analysis and other contemporary investigation techniques
* Ensuring corrective actions are practical, effective and embedded into business operations
* Maintaining compliance with legislative, regulatory and reporting requirements
* Managing safety records, reporting systems and digital safety management tools
* Developing safety metrics, reporting insights and recommendations to support business decision-making
* Driving continuous improvement across all safety and wellbeing programs

About You

You are more than a compliance professional, you are a genuine leader who can connect with people, earn trust and positively influence behaviours at every level of an organisation.

You will bring:

Essential Requirements

* Minimum Certificate IV in Work Health & Safety or Occupational Health & Safety
* Demonstrated experience in a similar Safety Manager, Safety Advisor or Health & Safety leadership role within manufacturing, industrial, logistics, warehousing, technical services or a comparable operational environment
* Experience as a Return to Work Coordinator
* Strong capability in risk management, safety systems and operational safety leadership
* Proven experience leading complex incident investigations and implementing sustainable corrective actions
* Excellent knowledge of reporting procedures, record-keeping requirements and safety management systems
* Strong understanding and application of digital reporting and safety management platforms

Comprehensive knowledge of:
* Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004 (Victoria)
* Victorian OHS Regulations
* Relevant Australian Standards and industry best practice
* Current driver's licence

Personal Attributes
We are looking for someone who:

* Leads with authenticity, integrity and accountability
* Has an open, approachable and engaging communication style
* Can confidently influence and coach leaders, supervisors and frontline employees
* Builds strong relationships across all levels of the organisation and with external stakeholders
* Balances commercial understanding with a genuine commitment to safety and legal compliance
* Is highly organised, proactive and solutions-focused
* Thrives in a hands-on environment and enjoys being visible in the workplace rather than behind a desk

Why Join Us?

* Attractive $100K++ salary and benefits package
* Key leadership position with genuine influence across the organisation
* Diverse operational environment providing variety and challenge
* Opportunity to shape safety culture and drive meaningful change
* Work with a business that values people, safety and continuous improvement
* Enjoy the lifestyle benefits of living and working in beautiful regional Wangaratta

Ready to Lead the Way?

If you're a people-first safety professional with the experience, credibility and passion to create safer workplaces and stronger safety cultures, we'd love to hear from you.

Contact Dan Sawyer for a PD and more information in confidence on 0403 899143

As a Senior Cyber and Operational Technology Security Engineer you will be at the heart of our security operations helping to safeguard the organisation from cyber threats. You will be responsible for the design, implementation and maintenance of the digital security systems and processes that protect our caregivers, patients, and information.

Additionally, you will be responsible for overseeing cyber security engineering of St John of God Health Care's Operational Technology (OT) - including facilities, clinical - medical operational technologies, and associated Internet of Things (IoT) devices - to protect, detect and respond to cyber threats across the organisation.

The Position

Building, operating, and continuously improving cybersecurity tools and processes

Act as the senior SME for integrated OT, cloud, and data security, providing authoritative technical guidance on secure architecture, design patterns, and control implementation.

Support the design and maintenance of OT security reference architectures aligned to Australian regulatory requirements and industry standards (including AS-IEC 62443 and Purdue principles), incorporating segmentation, DMZs, and least-privilege remote access.

Establish and maintain OT asset discovery and inventory using passive, protocol-aware techniques, and configure and tune monitoring and anomaly-detection capabilities in safety-critical environments.

Provide senior technical input to IT-OT network segmentation initiatives in collaboration with network, facilities, and engineering teams.

Provide technical oversight and integration guidance for enterprise security platforms (including SIEM, XDR-EDR, CASB, vulnerability management, and firewalls), including OT telemetry integration, in collaboration with SOC-MSSP providers.

Establish and maintain visibility, security baselines, and monitoring for IoT and connected devices supporting facilities and clinical operations, ensuring OT-safe methods that protect service continuity and safety.

Define and maintain OT-appropriate vulnerability, patching, cyber risk controls, and change management approaches that balance cyber risk reduction with clinical safety and service availability.

Define, implement and assure OT vendor and supply-chain security controls, including secure remote access patterns (jump hosts, MFA, time-bound access, monitoring), contractual security requirements, and validation of third-party controls for clinical and facilities technologies.

Lead OT cyber risk assessments and security uplift planning aligned to AS-IEC 62443 concepts (e.g., zone-conduit design and target security levels), ensuring risk treatments are practical for safety-critical operations and clinical environments.

Provide senior technical input into cyber incident preparedness and response across IT and OT environments, including developing OT-safe runbooks, supporting incident detection and remediation, and contributing to exercises and readiness assessments..

Coordinate with internal stakeholders and external vendors to investigate, resolve, and document incidents, ensuring root-cause analysis and lessons learned inform future improvements.

You will have demonstrated technical understanding and expertise in OT security and architecture, with demonstrated experience integrating OT controls with enterprise cyber security capabilities (e.g., SIEM-XDR, identity controls, and data protection-DLP) where OT systems interface with IT or cloud platforms. result.description:
About Us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory and beyond.

About the Employer
We are supporting an automotive business (ABN 69 669 060 913) based in Acacia Ridge, Queensland, specialising in Japanese vehicle imports, compliance, mechanical repairs, servicing, and vehicle inspections. With over 20 years of industry experience and a commitment to quality, safety, and customer satisfaction. The business is seeking a Motor Mechanic to support its growing operations and to maintain, test, diagnose and repair petrol engines and the mechanical components of lightweight motor vehicles, including transmissions, suspension, steering and braking systems.

Salary: $79,423 to $83,000 per annum plus superannuation
Location: Acacia Ridge, QLD
Employment Type: Full-time, ongoing
Ordinary Hours: 38 hours per week

Key Responsibilities
- Detect and diagnose mechanical and related electrical faults in petrol engines and vehicle components.
- Use automotive diagnostic scan tools, computers, multimeters, pressure gauges and other testing equipment to identify faults.
- Inspect and test petrol engines, transmissions, steering systems, suspension systems, brakes and related mechanical components.
- Dismantle and remove engine assemblies, transmissions, steering mechanisms and other mechanical components.
- Examine dismantled parts and components for wear, damage, defects and serviceability.
- Repair or replace worn, damaged and defective mechanical parts.
- Reassemble petrol engines and mechanical components following repairs.
- Test and adjust repaired mechanical components to confirm correct operation and performance.
- Perform scheduled maintenance services, including oil and filter changes, lubrication, fluid replacement and engine tune-ups.
- Diagnose and repair fuel, ignition, cooling and engine-management systems.
- Service and repair transmissions, steering, suspension and braking systems.
- Complete vehicle road tests and post-repair inspections.
- Confirm that repairs have been completed correctly and that vehicles operate safely.
- Follow manufacturer specifications, service manuals, technical bulletins and workshop procedures.
- Inspect vehicles for roadworthiness and identify repairs required to meet applicable roadworthiness standards.
- Issue roadworthiness or safety certificates where appropriately licensed or authorised.
- Respond to vehicle breakdown service calls where required.
- Accurately record diagnostic findings, repairs completed, parts used and further work recommended.
- Complete job cards, service records and workshop documentation.
- Safely operate vehicle hoists, mechanical tools, power tools and diagnostic equipment.
- Maintain a clean, safe and organised workshop.
- Comply with workplace health and safety and environmental requirements.
- Assist apprentices or junior workshop employees where reasonably required.

Selection Criteria
1. Light-vehicle mechanical expertise
Demonstrated experience maintaining and repairing petrol-powered passenger and light commercial vehicles.
2. Diagnostic skills
Ability to detect and diagnose mechanical and related electrical faults using automotive diagnostic equipment.
3. Mechanical repair skills
Experience repairing petrol engines, transmissions, brakes, steering and suspension systems.
4. Technical knowledge
Ability to understand and follow manufacturer specifications, service manuals and technical repair information.
5. Problem-solving ability
Ability to identify vehicle faults, determine suitable repair methods and resolve mechanical problems efficiently.
6. Quality workmanship
Strong attention to detail and commitment to completing repairs to an appropriate trade and safety standard.
7. Organisation
Ability to manage allocated workshop jobs, maintain accurate records and complete repairs within required timeframes.
8. Communication and teamwork
Ability to communicate repair findings clearly and work effectively with workshop staff, management and service personnel.
9. Safety awareness
Demonstrated understanding of workshop safety, safe equipment operation and environmentally responsible waste disposal.

Required Qualifications and Experience
- AQF Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology, AQF Certificate IV, or an equivalent recognised automotive mechanical qualification.
- Relevant practical experience servicing and repairing petrol-powered lightweight motor vehicles.
- At least three years of relevant experience
- Experience using automotive diagnostic scan tools and testing equipment.
- Experience diagnosing and repairing petrol engines and associated mechanical systems.
- Current driver licence.
- Ability to work full-time in Brisbane.

How to Apply
We are looking for a reliable, skilled, and safety-minded automotive professional to support vehicle servicing, repairs, inspections, and workshop operations while maintaining high standards of quality, efficiency, and customer service.

To apply, please submit the following:
- Resume outlining your work experience and references.
- A short cover letter of no more than 300 words explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork. Please use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
- A written response of no more than 600 words describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role. Please structure your example or examples using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a professional and growing automotive business that values quality, safety, teamwork, reliability, and customer satisfaction, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Phone calls and walk-in applications will not be accepted.

Applications Close: 13 August 2026
